uwp_capture_status: ok: original UWP app (PID 15288, window 'AudioCategory C# sample') built Release, launched, and captured. Note: nav list items render as 'N) Title' so bare-title navigation did not switch scenario pages in the UWP capture; all 10 baseline frames show the default (Movie) page. Per-scenario UWP source was used as ground truth.
capture_limitation: WinUI 3 desktop content could not be rasterised in this headless session (PrintWindow/GDI returns a blank surface for DirectComposition swapchains; UWP via ApplicationFrameHost captured normally). WinUI verdicts rely on the captured UIA tree + behavioural manifest + source review, which confirm all controls are present, named, and wired.
scoring_note: Structural gate (Compare-Parity) scored 0/100 because the checklist keyed on the exact UWP button label 'Select Audio File', which the migration renamed; functionally the equivalent control is present and wired in every scenario. Each scenario graded PARTIAL: present + functional but with visible text/description fidelity gaps and unverifiable pixel rendering. score = round(100*(0 + 0.5*10)/10) = 50.

features.name: Movie
features.note: Scenario present and navigable in WinUI; primary action button is wired (Default_Click sets MediaPlayerAudioCategory.Movie and opens a file picker) and PlaybackControl (Play/Pause/Stop + MediaPlayer + status) is fully implemented. Fidelity gaps vs UWP: (1) action button relabelled from 'Select Audio File' to 'Set Movie category and play a file'; (2) UWP 'Description:' paragraph dropped on the page. Action invocation produced no auto-detectable response in EITHER app (button opens a file picker) so no behavioural regression. WinUI screenshot is blank due to a headless DirectComposition capture limitation, not a blank app - the UIA tree enumerates all controls at real coordinates.
